The fetchedAt validation logic establishes a three-layered temporal integrity protocol within GSE. The first layer, row selection, enforces market-specific data semantics by ensuring that SPREAD-type odds are derived from batches with shared freshness timestamps, while H2H odds are sourced from their own respective rows. This prevents cross-market contamination of temporal signals. The second layer, candidate gate, applies a hard cutoff at 6 hours (21600 seconds) to reject stale odds, preventing erroneous inference in downstream systems. The third layer, ops monitor, classifies fetchedAt ages into operational statuses—ok, warn, alert, and gate breach—enabling proactive maintenance. These layers collectively form a dualistic structure: one that validates data freshness (candidate gate) and another that monitors operational health (ops monitor), both grounded in the invariant principle that fetchedAt reflects actual fetch time. Failure modes include misalignment between batch timestamps and individual row timestamps, or bypassing the 6-hour rule through backdating, which would compromise the integrity of the entire system.
